content: 1. Show your child affection and express your love openly and consistently. 2. Pay close attention to your child’s interests and actively respond to them. 3. Praise your child for their efforts when they attempt to learn new skills. 4. From birth, your baby begins to learn. Provide opportunities for your baby to see, hear, move their arms and legs freely, and touch you. 5. Gently soothe, stroke, and hold your baby. Skin-to-skin contact is highly beneficial. 6. Make eye contact with your baby and talk to them, especially during breastfeeding, as it is an excellent time for bonding and communication. 7. Offer your child opportunities to see, hear, feel, and move freely. Slowly move colorful objects for your child to observe and reach for. 8. Provide simple toys such as a shaker rattle or a large ring on a string to stimulate their senses and motor skills. 9. Smile and laugh with your child to foster emotional connection. 10. Engage in conversations with your child, even if they cannot yet respond with words. 11. Give your child clean and safe household items to explore, such as containers with lids, metal pots, and spoons, which they can handle, bang, or drop. 12. Respond to your child’s sounds and show interest in what captures their attention. 13. Hide your child’s favorite toy under a cloth or box and encourage them to find it. Play games like peek-a-boo to stimulate their cognitive development. 14. Teach your child the names of objects and people in their environment to build their vocabulary. 15. Provide your child with items they can stack, place into containers, and remove, such as nesting and stacking objects, containers, or clothespins. 16. Ask your child simple questions and respond to their attempts to communicate, encouraging their language development. 17. Help your child count, name, and compare objects. Create simple toys for them, such as items of different colors and shapes for sorting, or use tools like a chalkboard or puzzles. 18. Encourage your child to talk and answer their questions thoughtfully. 19. Teach your child stories, songs, and games to enhance their imagination and language skills. 20. Discuss pictures or books with your child to stimulate their curiosity and comprehension.
